claim: Lee Jackson (Planet FPL Aston Villa correspondent) says he wouldn't buy any Villa assets right now, waiting until around gameweek 9 depending on Fulham's form before investing in Villa's attack.
quote: I wouldn't be buying any Villa assets right now. I think like you say, I would watch and wait.

claim: Lee Jackson says Villa's defenders remain off the FPL menu even once the attack becomes buyable around gameweek 9.
quote: Villa defense still very much off the menu.

claim: Lee Jackson's preferred Villa midfield buy is Manzambi, though it's close with Buendia; he says it's still early to call him a nailed starter after only a game and a half.
quote: It is Manzambi for me but it's really tight.

claim: Lee Jackson rates Buendia as a good alternative to Manzambi, noting he scored goals last season and is trusted by Emery.
quote: I think Wendia um is a good option. We've seen last season he scores goals.

claim: Lee Jackson thinks Buendia is Villa's most likely penalty taker this season, with Nicolas Jackson the most likely alternative; Villa haven't had a clear taker since Douglas Luiz left and Tammy Abraham isn't first choice.
quote: So for me, it's probably Buendia. Uh it could be Jackson.

claim: Lee Jackson would not pick McGinn at 5.4 for FPL, expecting occasional goal involvement but not enough consistent returns compared with Manzambi or Buendia.
quote: I just don't think there's going to be enough consistent returns for him to be an FPL asset.

claim: Lee Jackson says Nicolas Jackson is Villa's clear first-choice striker and will start every match, citing Emery's trust from their time together at Villarreal.
quote: he's going to start every match for us. I think that's pretty clear as well.

claim: Lee Jackson isn't worried about Nicolas Jackson handling Villa's upcoming fixture-congested run including Champions League midweeks, noting he already played two games in a week and started in the cup.
quote: I think he's an Olly Watkins replacement. We want a a minutes monster that can do that pressing twice a week if needed.

claim: Lee Jackson sees Nicolas Jackson's 6.5 price as generous and thinks he could become an appealing option if Villa's service to him improves.
quote: I think 6.5 is a really generous price.

claim: Lee Jackson says Madjo won't be an immediate FPL threat once fit and Tammy Abraham will only get some minutes, with Nicolas Jackson remaining the clear first choice up front.
quote: I think Maja will get minutes and Tammy Abraham will get minutes but Nicholas Jackson is the clear first choice.

claim: Lee Jackson says Villa will concede more goals having lost Konsa (now at Arsenal), calling it a big factor behind their leakier defense.
quote: He was a big part in our defense and um we're going to concede more goals without him.

claim: Lee Jackson says Maatsen is out for three months.
quote: Matson's out for three months, I believe. So that's really disappointing.

claim: Lee Jackson says the player deputizing for the injured Maatsen (heard as 'Roger', taken here as Ruggeri - uncertain match) has looked okay generally, though Savio gave him a difficult first half against Tottenham.
quote: Roger looks okay. He's deputizing for Matson all right. Although Savia gave him a bit of a runaround in the first half against Tottenham.

claim: Lee Jackson says an injured Villa centre-back heard as 'Torres' (not matched on the roster) is the bigger defensive loss for playing out from the back, rating him levels above Mings in buildup play.
quote: Torres is the big one. The playing it out from the back um and buildup play, Torres is levels above Mings.

claim: Lee Jackson still sees Cash as Villa's number one right-back, benched at the weekend only as an injury precaution, but calls it a closer battle than expected with Wan-Bissaka playing well as deputy.
quote: I think Cash is still number one. Um he was on the bench at the weekend, but I think that's just because he's coming back from an injury.

claim: Asked which Villa defender he'd pick for FPL, Lee Jackson says Lindelof for the safest minutes.
quote: Probably Lindelof.

claim: Lee Jackson describes a player heard as 'Harwood Bellis' (not matched on the current roster) as a longer-term fourth-choice centre-back project for Villa, not yet a starter ahead of Lindelof.
quote: I think Harwood Bellis has been bought as a longerterm prospect.

claim: Lee Jackson says Garnacho has gone from getting 10-15 minute cameos to not featuring at all, cautiously speculating it could become a Harvey Elliott-style freeze-out given how demanding Emery is on the training ground.
quote: he played like 10, 15 minutes in a few games and now it's like he's on the bench every single game and he's not coming on at all.

claim: Lee Jackson describes Alysson (caption rendered 'Allison'; resolved from context as the Villa attacker, not Liverpool's A.Becker) as a pacey, direct, take-a-man type attacking option who is exciting.
quote: he's a an umbai a Gacho type that will try and beat a man. Pacey will take risks.

claim: Projecting a month ahead once everyone is fit, Lee Jackson sees Villa's attack as Jackson at 9, Manzambi in the 10 role, Buendia or Alysson wide, McGinn on the other side, and Kamara/Gomes as the double pivot - not Goretzka, who isn't fit yet.
quote: I think Manzambi is definitely going to be in that number 10 behind Jackson when he's fit.

claim: Lee Jackson says Hemmings is fine to hold or pick as a cheap 4.5 filler who Emery clearly trusts, but he's not confident Hemmings keeps his starting spot as Villa's other attacking options get integrated.
quote: If he's in your squad, it's fine. Keep him. If you're on wild card and you need a 4.5, it's fine. He'll get minutes.

claim: Lee Jackson is very impressed with new Villa goalkeeper Suzuki, praising his distribution (maybe better than predecessor Martinez) and several good stops against Tottenham.
quote: throwing and kicking looks really really good in terms of those long balls, maybe better than Martinez in terms of distribution.

claim: Suzuki will miss Villa games in January while away with Japan at the Asia Cup, since he's their number one.
quote: we are going to lose Suzuki to the Asia Cup because he's the Japan number one.

claim: Lee Jackson says he wouldn't pay 0.5m more for Suzuki over a set-and-forget 4.5m keeper even if guaranteed nailed all season, given the coming Asia Cup absence.
quote: Even if you tell me Suzuki is going to play every game the rest of the season, I just don't think he's worth.5 more than a 4.5 million keeper.

claim: The host notes most managers won't play a second wildcard until around gameweek 32, so a goalkeeper picked now needs to cope with Suzuki's January Asia Cup absence without a wildcard bailout.
quote: You're probably not going to wild card to round about game week 32 or so. You are going to lose him for a bit, aren't you, Lee?

claim: Lee Jackson predicts a 1-1 draw between Villa and Brentford, saying he isn't confident Villa win.
quote: I don't think we'll win. I'm going to say 1-1.

claim: Tom (Planet FPL Brentford correspondent) predicts a 2-1 Brentford win over Villa.
quote: I think we're going to do it. Yeah. 2-1 to us.

claim: Tom says Schade's minutes are rock solid even after Anthony's arrival, since Anthony has settled on the right rather than challenging Schade's left-sided role.
quote: I mean just minutes are so solid at the moment.

claim: Tom calls Lewis-Potter an underrated player who consistently gets into great positions, crediting him with the buildup for a glorious chance that led to Schade's goal against Chelsea.
quote: he's such an underrated player. Um but he's just getting in all the right positions.

claim: Tom notes Thiago's goal against Chelsea came from a chance he 'shouldn't have scored', while a clearer opening went to waste - a reminder that recent returns aren't a clean read of his chance quality.
quote: Shardai should have scored and Thiago shouldn't have scored that. So, yeah, that's a shard golden assist and a Thiago blank again.

claim: The host cites a stat that Lewis-Potter has a higher xGI than Schade so far this season, after having the highest xG of any Brentford midfielder last season.
quote: he's got a higher xGI than Kevin Shard so far this season.

claim: Tom is certain Lewis-Potter starts at left-back against Villa this gameweek, but has no idea where he'll be playing (left-back, bench, or further forward) a few weeks beyond that as other signings get integrated.
quote: I'm pretty sure he'll be starting left back against Villa, but the game after does he I don't know. I don't know.

claim: Tom says Sangare's minutes will keep being managed as he settles into the league; he was surprised to see him benched against Chelsea and thinks he starts against Villa after the international break, but it's just as likely he's on the bench or gets only 45 minutes.
quote: it's also at the moment quite as likely that he could start on the bench or have 45 minutes.

claim: Tom says if he weren't on wildcard he'd hold Sangare rather than transfer him out.
quote: if I wasn't, I'd probably just stick it out and keep him.

claim: Tom, building his own wildcard squad, is leaving Sangare out in favour of Schade.
quote: I mean, I may as well have Yeah, I'm sure talking about Kevin Shard at 6.2 and scoring goals and playing as many minutes as everybody else.

claim: Tom says Yarmoliuk is only worth buying if Sangare or Janelt gets injured; despite being capable of defensive contributions he hasn't hit the DefCon threshold in any game this season.
quote: if Yan out or Sangari get injured, then absolutely feel free to steam into Yamalook, but at the moment there I don't see there's no reason to.

claim: Tom says Janelt has played every minute so far and is good for DefCon points (roughly four to five a week including a clean sheet), but his attacking returns from last year were poor and he's mainly a bench eighth-attacker at 5.0m.
quote: He's played every minute of every game so far.

claim: Tom notes Milambo is being worked back into the picture from the under-21s, adding to the competition for Brentford's central midfield spots alongside Sangare and Janelt.
quote: Anthony Milambo is now playing uh he was playing under 21 the other day and obviously we signed him last year to sort of be integrated into the first team.

claim: Tom says Dango Ouattara's game time has become unpredictable since Anthony's arrival - left out then impressive off the bench against Leeds, back in the XI, then out again - with Anthony now the pick on the right.
quote: he was left out leads He came on, he performed really well. He was back in, he was back out.

claim: Tom says Dango Ouattara has the same points total as Fabio Carvalho so far and is a sell if owned right now, given Anthony's impact on his minutes.
quote: he's got the same amount of points as Fabio Cavalio at the moment. So yeah, definitely a cell if you got him.

claim: Tom rates Anthony as currently the pick of Brentford's wide options, settled on the right.
quote: Antony's obviously coming in and playing on the right hand side um it just at the moment it just seems that he's sort of the the pick of the bunch.

claim: Tom still calls Kayode first choice at right-back despite a rough recent stretch (subbed at half-time vs Sunderland, benched vs Bournemouth, hooked with 25 minutes left vs Chelsea), rating him a level above Hickey.
quote: Kaido is definitely first choice still.

claim: Tom says there's no rush to sell Kayode at around 4.5-4.6m, expecting him to keep starting.
quote: there's no rush to get rid of him. I think he will still play. He's definitely still first choice.

claim: Tom expects Ajer to keep starting and Collins to return alongside him after the international break, with impressive deputy Schuster (a DefCon vs Sunderland among his cameos) dropping back to cup duty rather than staying a league starter; Van den Berg is further away and won't be rushed.
quote: Christopher Aair will still be playing I reckon

claim: Tom has owned Ajer since the start of the season and is very comfortable keeping him.
quote: I've had I've had him since the start.

claim: Tom, who owns Thiago, says his underlying xG has actually been pretty good despite the lack of goals (blanks vs Sunderland/Leeds, a penalty miss vs Leeds), and now that he's scored his first league goal (vs Chelsea) expects him to kick on; Tom is keeping him on wildcard.
quote: if you look at his like xG over the season's actually been pretty good.

claim: Tom speculates Thiago may have taken a confidence knock from a poor World Cup appearance for Brazil against Morocco, after which the manager dropped him, possibly explaining his slow start to the season.
quote: maybe he took a bit of a knock to the confidence cuz I mean he went into the World Cup obviously you know second top scorer in the Prem.

claim: Lee Jackson says he's now interested in Thiago given his price has dropped, especially once Brentford's good fixtures arrive, calling him an under-the-radar option.
quote: I'm just interested in Thiago, especially now he's dropped a bit in price um when those good fixtures come around.

claim: Tom's overall verdict on Brentford's midfield assets for FPL is to pick Schade on a wildcard and ignore the rest.
quote: and just ignore the rest.

claim: The host references Joao Pedro's injury situation as a live factor in whether Thiago was a tougher early-season pick than him, without giving new detail on a return timeline.
quote: if Pedro's injury situation changes, but I think Thiago was a tough pick over Xiao Pedro to start the season.
